transcript_header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Ethan Ross (CTO - Solaris), Priya Singh (Lead Engineer), Avery Cole (PM)
summary: Quick SDK walkthrough for Redwood API and Console focused on Python/TypeScript quickstarts, auth options (API keys vs SSO/KMS), environment setup, and next steps for a POC. Customer wants low latency for 3-5 concurrent flows, concerns about data residency and KMS integration. AE/SE will provide quickstarts, security docs, and schedule POC benchmarks.
topics: Intro & goals; Quickstart (Python/TS) code walkthrough; Auth & secrets management (API key, SSO, KMS); Environment & deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private); Console demo (routes, billing, logs); Performance considerations (batching, quantization); Next steps and action items
transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, it's Liam from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ethan: Ethan here, CTO at Solaris.
[00:08] Priya: Priya, engineering.
[00:09] Avery: Avery, product.
[00:10] Sofia: Sofia, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:12] Liam: Cool, the goal today is a short SDK integration walkthrough — Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth, and environment setup. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:25] Ethan: Sounds good. Our main ask: low latency for payment routing and fraud scoring, and we need to understand how auth/security works - especially KMS and VPC options.
[00:35] Liam: Perfect. Sofia, do you want to kick off the code walkthrough?
[00:38] Sofia: Yeah absolutely. I'll share my screen — give me a sec. (screen shares) Ok, starting with Python quickstart, this is the minimal pip package usage: import redwood, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env, then client = redwood.Client() and client.chat.create(...) — pretty straight forward.
[01:02] Priya: Quick Q, we run containers in our prod cluster and use HashiCorp Vault, would the SDK pick up env var keys or do we need a special adapter?
[01:10] Sofia: The SDK will read from REDWOOD_API_KEY env var by default, but we also support passing a token programmatically. For Vault you can fetch keys at container startup and inject into env, or use our short-lived token flow with your identity provider via SAML/OIDC to mint tokens — that integrates with KMS for envelope encryption if you want.
[01:32] Liam: To add, for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed KMS and you can bring your own key material. Public hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys unless you opt into a dedicated KMS config.
[01:45] Avery: Is that an add-on or included in enterprise plans?
[01:48] Liam: Typically part of Private deployments or enterprise contracts, it's available as a configuration. We'll send exact packaging in the follow-up.
[01:55] Sofia: Back to the quickstart — TypeScript is similar, npm install @redwoodai/sdk, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, then const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) and client.generate({ model: 'rw-text-1', prompt }) — we have helpers for streaming and also for structured outputs.
[02:22] Ethan: Any gotchas for streaming in Node? We do real-time scoring and want small tail latencies.
[02:28] Sofia: For streaming, reduce chunk size and use the SDK's onToken callback to process as tokens arrive. Also consider our 'low-latency' routing tier if you need guaranteed p99.
[02:38] Priya: How do we set up environment separation — dev/staging/prod — with keys and rate limits?
[02:45] Liam: We recommend separate API keys per environment and per service account plus route-level quotas in the Console. We'll demo that in a sec.
[02:55] Sofia: Jumping to Console: here's the Projects page, you can create projects, assign API keys, and bind keys to routes with different limits. You can also pin models per-route and set fallback policies.
[03:15] Priya: Can we restrict keys to IP ranges or VPC connectors?
[03:20] Sofia: Yes, on Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and IP allowlists. Hosted API has key scoping and route restrictions, but if you need network isolation, Dedicated or Private is the path.
[03:33] Ethan: Data retention — what's the default? We process PCI-adjacent data so need clarity about logs.
[03:39] Liam: By default, hosted logs are retained 30 days and used for debugging, but for enterprise you can enable no-retention or customer-controlled retention. For PCI-like workloads we'd recommend Private with audit-logging integrated to your SIEM.
[03:55] Avery: Can you show where to find usage/cost dashboards?
[03:59] Sofia: Sure, under Observability -> Token usage you get token-level breakdowns, per-route latencies, and cost estimates. There are also export hooks into BigQuery or S3 for longer retention.
[04:12] Priya: Great. For the SDK install, are there size or dependency issues for our lambdas? We like small bundles.
[04:18] Sofia: SDK is lightweight; the core client is a small wrapper. For extreme size constraints we have a minimal fetch-based helper that just posts to the REST endpoint. We'll share both options.
[04:28] Liam: Let's talk auth flows quickly — simplest is static API key; recommended for prod is short-lived tokens minted via SSO/OpenID Connect. We can show an example with AWS STS + OIDC or with your existing IdP. Also KMS/envelope encryption for payloads at rest.
[04:49] Ethan: If we want to do on-prem, what's the gap to full private deployment? We might need that for compliance.
[04:55] Sofia: Private deployment is a packaged control plane you host in your VPC — supports customer-managed KMS, SSO, audit logs, and on-prem air-gapped options. It typically takes a few weeks to stand up with our deploy team. For a POC you can start on Hosted or Dedicated to validate latency and correctness.
[05:12] Priya: Can you run a quick code run? Just show the basics of a request and a streaming callback in Node.
[05:18] Sofia: Sure. (types) const res = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rw-chat-1', messages: [...] , onToken: token => { process.stdout.write(token) } }) — that's the pattern. We've got webhooks and async job APIs for long running tasks too.
[05:36] Ethan: How do you handle batching? We sometimes batch scoring for throughput.
[05:40] Sofia: Redwood runtime supports automatic batching up to a tunable batch size. In the SDK you can switch to batching mode or call the batch endpoint; runtime does KV cache and prefix caching to reduce tokens and improve latency. We'll include recommended configs based on your QPS.
[05:58] Avery: Any notes on quantization or model size tradeoffs? We have cost constraints.
[06:03] Sofia: We recommend quantized variants for throughput; Console Optimize will show model/quantization recommendations per workload. For strict low-latency path use higher-tier models pinned on Dedicated.
[06:14] Liam: Quick note on pricing — hosted usage is per-token; Dedicated is reserved capacity. We'll include an example cost calc for your workload after you share expected QPS and average prompt/response length.
[06:30] Priya: Ok, we can provide sample payloads. For the POC, what's the best way to measure latency and end-to-end?
[06:37] Sofia: Use our SDK with real request replay, or run the benchmark harness we provide — it's a small script that replays your sample traffic and reports p50/p95/p99 and cost. We'll share it.
[06:47] Liam: We'll also run a short internal benchmark with our test tokens against a similar model to give you an initial expectation.
[06:53] Ethan: Security — what about encryption at rest for logs?
[06:57] Liam: On Hosted we encrypt at rest with Redwood-managed KMS; for Private or Dedicated you can supply your own KMS key. Logs can be forwarded encrypted to your S3 or SIEM.
[07:07] Priya: Is SOC2 in scope?
[07:09] Liam: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We'll attach the summary and audit report in the follow-up.
[07:15] Sofia: Ok switching back to the SDK quickstarts — showing repo structure now, tests, and an example that uses environment variables and dotenv for local dev. The demo repo has two folders, python/ and ts/, each with minimal app and README.
[07:35] Priya: If we want to run the Python example in a container, any runtime env specifics?
[07:40] Sofia: Python needs requests + redwood package; set REDWOOD_API_KEY at container runtime. If using Vault, fetch and export before starting process. For async use we recommend uvicorn + async client.
[07:53] Avery: Do you have snippets for token rotation?
[07:56] Sofia: Yes, in the security doc we'll include short-lived token patterns and a sample Lambda that mints tokens using your IdP.
[08:05] Ethan: Can we limit model choices per key to prevent accidental large-model usage?
[08:09] Sofia: Yes, route/model pinning and key scoping can restrict which models a key can call.
[08:14] Priya: About observability, do you give trace ids we can connect to our tracing?
[08:18] Sofia: We surface request ids in response headers and you can forward traces into Datadog or Zipkin via export hooks.
[08:26] Liam: Any other questions on the SDK itself?
[08:28] Ethan: One more — offline testing for ML teams, can we download model artefacts?
[08:32] Liam: For open models we can provide weights for private deployments under a license; otherwise we offer hosted endpoints. We'll discuss license and network options in follow-up.
[08:42] Priya: For the quickstarts, how do we integrate with our CI/CD to avoid leaking keys?
[08:46] Sofia: Use CI secrets and rotate keys per pipeline. We also have a principle of least privilege for keys and recommend short lived tokens for pipelines.
[08:56] Avery: Ok, let's recap next steps — Liam?
[08:59] Liam: Sure: we'll send the quickstart repo link, Python and TS snippets, the security deck and SOC2 summary, and a benchmark harness. You'll provision a sandbox API key and Priya will share sample traffic. We'll schedule the POC benchmark next week.
[09:20] Ethan: Good. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[09:23] Liam: None, just waiting on your sample payloads and confirmation of a date.
[09:28] Priya: We'll aim to get that by Jan 5.
[09:30] Avery: Thanks folks, that was helpful.
[09:32] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email with the links.
[09:36] Liam: Closing — thanks all.

Notes: Transcript occasionally has slight ASR mis-hears (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K V cache', 'SAML' as 'Samuel'). References to dashboards are links in the follow-up email rather than embedded here.
